title: Web Standards: Compact Proof Timeline
description: A compact official-source timeline used to prove that the evidence engine works beyond company and product histories.

events.title: The World Wide Web is proposed
events.summary: Tim Berners-Lee wrote Information Management: A Proposal at CERN, describing a distributed hypertext system for managing complex evolving information.

sources.title: Information Management: A Proposal
sources.claim_scope: Original web proposal and distributed-hypertext framing

events.interpretation: This is an example of a timeline beginning with a primary artifact rather than a product announcement.
events.capability_implication: The proposal describes linked information as a way to navigate complex, evolving systems.

events.title: The World Wide Web Consortium is founded
events.summary: Tim Berners-Lee founded W3C in October 1994 to foster a consistent architecture for the rapidly growing web.
events.interpretation: The timeline shifts from an initial technical proposal to an institution for interoperable standards.
events.social_implication: Open standards require durable institutions and multi-stakeholder participation.

events.title: WCAG 2.0 becomes a W3C Recommendation
events.summary: W3C published Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 as a stable, referenceable Recommendation web standard.

sources.title: WCAG 2 Overview
sources.claim_scope: WCAG version publication dates and backwards-compatibility explanation

events.interpretation: This demonstrates how the same engine can track standards and public-interest guidance rather than software releases.
events.social_implication: Accessibility standards make the web's human consequences part of the historical record.

events.title: WCAG 2.1 is published
events.summary: W3C published WCAG 2.1, adding one guideline and 17 success criteria while preserving backwards compatibility with WCAG 2.0.

sources.title: WCAG 2 Overview
sources.claim_scope: WCAG 2.1 publication date and added criteria

events.interpretation: This shows an evolving standards branch with continuity across versions.
events.social_implication: The newer recommendation expands accessibility coverage without discarding the earlier baseline.

events.title: WCAG 2.2 becomes a W3C Recommendation
events.summary: W3C published WCAG 2.2 as a Recommendation, adding nine success criteria since WCAG 2.1.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation
sources.claim_scope: WCAG 2.2 Recommendation publication and added success criteria

sources.title: WCAG 2 Overview
sources.claim_scope: WCAG version relationships and backwards compatibility

events.interpretation: A standards timeline can retain version relationships and compatibility context directly beside the dated event.
events.social_implication: The added criteria improve accessibility guidance for people with visual, physical, and cognitive disabilities.
